newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo to boost Brazil soy exports from north port.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo to boost Brazil soy exports from north port.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Thursday that it would increase soybean shipments from Brazil's northern port of Itacoatiara rather than from the traditional ports of Santos and Paranagua.
The trading house said in a statement that the decision was made because of cheaper transportation costs from the growing regions.
It has already bought 35,000 tonnes of soybean for shipment in June 1997 from Itacoatiara.
"Transportation costs to Itacoatiara are up to $20 per tonne cheaper than going to the southern ports," a Sumitomo Corp official said.
"We plan to ship more than half of our soybean purchases from Itacoatiara from 1998, rather than from other southern ports such as Paranagua," the Sumitomo official said.
The trade house opened the bean shipment route through Itacoatiara in cooperation with Brazilian grain firm Sementes Maggi Ltd.
